Fourier transforms convert midpoint product into ordinary convolution followed by tau=g/2, yielding exact cycle equations c_chi=c_(sigma chi)^2. On each sigma-cycle length l, roots w=0 or w^(2^l-1)=1 yield 2^l independent complex solutions. Reality is c_(chi^-1)=conj(c_chi); on a self-dual nontrivial orbit inversion is a half-cycle shift and forces w^(2^h+1)=1, giving 2^h+2 total including zero; distinct orbit pairs contribute 2^l. In an active Peirce block, multiplying cycle idempotency identities gives product weight=1; the weighted cyclic permutation has characteristic polynomial t^l-1, inactive block t^l. Independent modular orbit computations checked predicted real/complex counts for cyclic orders 1,3,5,7,9,11,13 and noncyclic C3^2. These do not independently verify all numerical quandle-basis eigenvalues but algebraic argument establishes generality.
